sections.title: Island overview
paragraphs: Erangel is an 8 × 8 km battleground combining settlements, farmland, hills and a southern military island. The official location guide highlights Stalber, Georgopol, Pochinki and Military Base. These are useful orientation points rather than promises of uncontested loot.

sections.title: A first rotation plan
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: choose a landing compound, one backup compound and the first route toward the safe zone before jumping. After landing, recheck the actual circle and transport options. Treat bridges and open fields as route decisions, and explain the next destination to teammates instead of chasing every gunshot.

sections.title: Terrain and special features
paragraphs: The official map page lists ferries, the UAZ and Secret Rooms as notable features. Use the linked gallery to recognise the landscape, then verify feature availability in the match you entered. A showcase page does not specify every ranked, custom or temporary-event rule.

sections.title: How to enter the map
paragraphs: Erangel is selected through the game’s available queues, map service or custom-match options, not acquired as an inventory item. Check the live lobby for your region and PC/console platform. Old patch schedules are historical evidence and must not be shown as today’s active rotation.

sections.title: Current layouts and evidence
paragraphs: Erangel’s visuals have changed over time. When following a route image, compare the building shape and surrounding roads against your client. This dossier provides a navigation framework, not exact loot spawns, a current ranked rotation or a claim that every old screenshot matches today’s map.

sections.title: Desert map identity
paragraphs: Miramar is an 8 × 8 km desert battleground. Its open views, ridges and towns create different navigation problems from Erangel’s greener landscape. The official guide highlights Partona, Resort, Truck Stop and the southern island as locations to recognise.

sections.title: Read the ridgeline
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: plan travel from cover to cover and identify the next ridge before moving. Stop to look from a position where you can retreat, rather than standing on the skyline. When comparing two routes, record exposure and travel time; a shorter straight line is not automatically the better route.

sections.title: Sandstorm and traversal
paragraphs: Update 25.1 documented the Sandstorm and ziplines. The storm affects visibility and health; ziplines provide marked travel routes. Treat these as features to check in the current match, not guarantees that a photographed route is safe or that an old equipment interaction remains unchanged.

sections.title: Queue and map service
paragraphs: Use your platform’s live lobby to determine whether Miramar is offered through selection, rotation or a custom match. A guide can explain the map without controlling the matchmaking pool. PC and console rollout schedules have differed in official patch notes.

sections.title: Recognise renamed places
paragraphs: Partona replaced Los Higos and Truck Stop replaced Junkyard in the documented 25.1 revision. If an older guide uses those names, compare its map date before navigating. No fixed vehicle spawn, secret guaranteed route or current best landing spot is asserted here.

history.label: Update 25.1 · Miramar revision

sections.title: Taego landmarks
paragraphs: Taego is an 8 × 8 km map with varied environments, including reed fields and the Ho San Prison area. The official guide also highlights Terminal, Buk San Sa and School. Learn the names together with the shapes of compounds so a team callout identifies an actual location.

sections.title: A route with a fallback
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: choose a compound with a clear exit, then decide which nearby terrain you will use if the circle shifts away. Check open approaches before committing to a building. A useful practice note records where your team could regroup, not only where the strongest item happened to appear once.

sections.title: Documented map features
paragraphs: The official map page lists Multi Care Packages, the K2 and Self AED. Taego’s launch notes described the K2 as a 5.56 mm rifle and introduced Self AED and Comeback BR. These establish feature history; they do not prove that the original revive rules remain active in every present-day mode.

sections.title: Entering Taego
paragraphs: Look at the current map service in the PC or console lobby. The launch-era Featured Map queue and mode list in Update 12.2 are historical, not instructions to find the same menu today. Use your live region and playlist when planning a team session.

sections.title: Revive and loot assumptions
paragraphs: Check the active rules before relying on a return-to-battle feature. A map gallery is for visual identification, not a promise of a Self AED, a guaranteed crate or a safe landing. This article has been source-reviewed but does not claim a current PC/console gameplay test.
